01-verification-code.title: The verification code will never be passed on: the most common and deadly entrance to account hacking
01-verification-code.excerpt: The six-digit registration code is equal to the account key. Requesting codes from acquaintances, prompting codes from fake customer service, and filling in codes at fishing sites—they are all essentially the same knife. This article explains the art of speech, principles and refusal of speech in one go.
01-verification-code.body:
If you could only remember one WhatsApp anti-theft rule, remember this one:Never tell anyone the verification code, and don't enter it on any "official-looking" webpage.When police and cybersecurity agencies in many places around the world report WhatsApp account takeover cases, they almost always list "scamming six-digit verification codes" at the top of the list. The reason is simple - WhatsApp uses the mobile phone number as the account identity, and the registration code in the text message or voice message is the key to "prove that you are the owner" on the new device.

Many people mistakenly believe that hacking accounts must require advanced hacking skills. In reality, the vast majority of successful cases rely onsocial engineering: Scammers use trust, courtesy, a sense of urgency, and a "do me a favor" mentality to get you to hand over the keys yourself. Once the verification code is obtained, the other party can complete the registration on their mobile phone, kick you offline, and then pretend to be you to deceive the next person.

What exactly is the verification code?

When you or anyone tries to log in/register for WhatsApp using a mobile number, a registration code, usually six digits, is sent to the number (which may also be announced via a voice call). Entering this string of numbers correctly is equivalent to telling WhatsApp: "The person who holds this SIM and can receive the text message is the account owner."

Therefore, it belongs to the same type of sensitive information as bank card dynamic passwords and email two-step verification codes. The difference is: once WhatsApp's verification code is abused, the loss is often not just "an App", but your entire address book, group chat trust relationships, and the financial risk of relatives and friends who may be defrauded again.

What are the most common words used by scammers?

The words will change, but the structure rarely changes. The following sentences have appeared repeatedly in police information bulletins in many countries in recent years:

  • "The verification code was sent to your mobile phone by mistake. Please help me get back those six numbers." - This is a serial scam that is common after an acquaintance's account has been stolen.
  • "I am WhatsApp/Meta/Customer Service, your account is abnormal, please send me the verification code to unblock it." - Officials will not ask for codes like this.
  • "Bank risk control/courier loss/tax refund requires you to provide WhatsApp verification code for verification." - Cross-channel impersonation.
  • "Voting, lottery, and questionnaire only take 10 seconds" - the fake site first collects your mobile phone number, and then the SMS code you just received.
  • "I helped your friend sign up for the lottery, and he sent you the verification code. Just forward it to me." - Involving you in other people's scam narratives.

There is only one judgment standard:As long as the other party's goal is to "get the WhatsApp registration code that just appeared on your phone," no matter how touching or urgent the story is, or how familiar the other party's avatar is, it will be treated as a stolen account.

Why “asking for code for acquaintances” is particularly dangerous

Scammers rarely use unknown numbers to deceive you right away. A more efficient approach is to capture A first, and then use A's chat window to find B. When B sees a familiar name and avatar, his defenses will immediately drop. After B hands over the verification code, the scammer gets B and then deceives C - formingAddress Book Infectious Diseases.

So when you receive a verification code from a "friend", the correct response is not "He is usually fine, so he should be fine", but:His number may no longer be in his possession.Please use the phone to call the original number in your address book instead, or confirm in person. Do not use the "new number" temporarily sent by the other party to call back as the only means of verification.

Correct rejection skills (can be copied directly)

  • "I will not send the verification code to anyone, including relatives. If you are really who you are, call me."
  • "WhatsApp officially doesn't ask for verification codes. I treat this as a scam."
  • "I can't assist in transcoding. You can just log in to your account again."

You can block or report them after you finish speaking, without further explanation. Scammers rely on dragging you into long conversations to make you feel embarrassed to say no.

If you have already sent the code

  1. Immediately open WhatsApp on this machine, try to re-verify the login with your own number, and kick the other party offline.
  2. After successful login, check "Associated Devices" and log out of all unknown sessions.
  3. Reset your 2-step verification PIN and confirm that the recovery email is still yours.
  4. Immediately notify relatives and friends: Ignore any borrowing money, code request, or voting links sent by "you".
  5. If a transfer loss has occurred, contact your bank and consider calling the police.

summary

The verification code is not "just any number", but account sovereignty. HoldLine puts this in the first article because it blocks the largest attack surface, is the lowest cost, and is the easiest to teach to family members. Develop "don't give it to anyone who wants it" into a muscle reaction, and then all the advanced settings will really work.

02-two-step-verification.title: The Complete Guide to Two-Step Verification: PINs, Recovery Emails, and Common Pitfalls
02-two-step-verification.excerpt: After turning on two-step verification, the SMS code alone is often not enough. This article explains step-by-step how to open it, how to set a PIN, why you can’t save your email address, and what to do if you are preempted to set a PIN.
02-two-step-verification.body:
Two-step verification is the basic protection that WhatsApp officials repeatedly recommend. Its core idea is simple: even if the scammer temporarily gets your SMS verification code, you will still need an additional PIN (or password for subsequent upgrades) when the new device is registered. Without a second door, takeover costs will rise significantly.

Many users "heard that they wanted to open it" but kept putting it off, or opened it but skipped the mailbox. As a result, when something really happened, it was either impossible to prevent, or the recovery process was delayed for several days. This article writes down the complete approach and pitfalls at once.

What can it protect against and what can’t it protect against?

Can significantly enhance:The other party tries to use your number to re-register on another mobile phone; the remediation window after you briefly leak the SMS code; and the success rate of "only relying on deceptive codes" is reduced.

Cannot be solved alone:You have told the other party your PIN; a Trojan horse peeked at the screen of your phone in real time; you actively scanned the other party's associated QR code (the Trojan was hooked on the web page); you lent your unlocked phone to others to operate at will.

Therefore, two-step verification is a "necessary but not sufficient" condition: it must be turned on, but it must also cooperate with verification code discipline and related equipment inspections.

Open path (subject to common versions)

  1. Open WhatsApp and enterset up.
  2. pointAccount→two-step verification.
  3. Select Enable and follow the prompts to create a 6-digit PIN (some regions/versions may prompt you to set a stronger password).
  4. Confirm PIN again.
  5. Add toAn email address that you can log in to permanentlyas a recovery method and complete email verification (if applicable).

The menu copy of different mobile phone brands may be slightly different (for example, entering settings from the avatar), but the logic of "Account → Two-step verification" is usually stable. If you can't find it, use the in-app search for the "two-step" keyword.

How to set PIN

  • Do not use birthdays, anniversaries, license plates, mobile phone numbers, or ID fragments.
  • Do not use patterns such as 123456, 000000, 888888, and 112233.
  • Do not use the same WeChat/Alipay/bank card/email password or simply change it.
  • It is recommended to write it in a password manager, or write it in an offline location where only you can see it; do not send it to the group for "backup".

The goal of a PIN is not to be "so easy to remember that you don't have to write it down", but rather "that others can't guess it and can't cheat it." You can keep it if you can’t remember it, but don’t set a weak password because of this.

Why recovery email is almost required

After turning on two-step verification, if you forget your PIN, the official process often relies on your registered email address to assist in resetting it; if there is no available email address, you may need to wait for a while (commonly described in public information as up to about seven days) before you can continue without a PIN. What's worse is that the hacker turns on the two-step verification first and binds their email, so you will be even more passive when you take it back.

Therefore, the email address must satisfy:

  • It is one that you use for a long time and can receive mail.
  • The email itself also has a strong password and two-step verification.
  • Do not use an email address that has been abandoned, is about to be cleared by the company, or is shared with others.

What should I do after opening it?

  1. Check "Associated Devices" immediately and clear unknown sessions.
  2. Tell your family: The PIN for two-step verification cannot be shared with “customer service” either.
  3. Every few months or after switching devices, make sure two-step verification is still on.
  4. If you ever suspect a leak, just turn it off and on again to get a new PIN.

Asked for a "PIN I didn't set up"

This usually means: Someone took control of your account and enabled two-step verification. Please complete the SMS registration code verification first (this step can often kick the other party's main session offline), and then follow the interface prompts to process the PIN. For detailed emergency information, please see the "Unfamiliar PIN" topic on this site. The core principles are:Don’t give up on re-verification just because your PIN is stuck; don’t send SMS codes to people claiming to help you “crack your PIN.”

summary

Two-step verification takes less than two minutes, but it can turn "you can steal an account by cheating once with a text message code" into "you have to go through the door you set again." Together with recovery email and verification code discipline, it is one of the "must be done today" items recommended by HoldLine.

03-linked-devices.title: The Complete Guide to Connected Devices: How to Spot Silent Peeping
03-linked-devices.excerpt: Just because a mobile phone can still chat normally does not mean that there is no second pair of eyes. Once the web version/PC version is connected, the other party can synchronize in real time. Teach you how to check, kick, and avoid getting hit again.
03-linked-devices.body:
There is a kind of account hacking that is not dramatic: you are not suddenly logged out, and the chat is still there, until one day a relative or friend says, "You just asked me for a verification code," or you see a browser session in the settings that you never recognize. this isSilent access of associated devices——The attacker does not necessarily take away the main session of the phone, but allows WhatsApp Web/Desktop to hang on the side to synchronize messages.

For scammers, this method is extremely cost-effective: the later you find out, the more group chats they can read, the more materials they can collect for money-loaning techniques, and even directly use your tone of voice to operate in the conversation.

A brief description of the associated device mechanism

WhatsApp allows you to associate computers, tablets, browsers, etc. as companion devices in addition to the main client on your phone. The formal usage is: Open "Associated Devices" → "Associate New Device" on your mobile phone, and then scan the QR code displayed on the official website or desktop application.

The risk point is that this "code scanning authorization" process itself is a legal function. All the liar has to do is toThe QR code they controlPut it on a fake website, fake voting page, or scan the code directly on your unlocked phone.

How to check (please do it now)

  1. Open WhatsApp →set up→Linked devices(Android sometimes has the More menu in the upper right corner).
  2. Look at each entry in the list: device type, approximate active time, and whether the name looks familiar.
  3. For any "I don't remember linking" items: Click through →Exit/Logout.
  4. If the list is very long and you have logged in from a public computer, it is recommended that all unfamiliar users log out and reconnect with the official website if necessary.

Make it a habit: Take 30 seconds to scan your list one day a week (like Sunday night). After lending your phone, clicking on a suspicious link, or using the hotel computer, check again immediately.

List of high-risk scenarios

  • Scanned the "Verify/Vote/Receive Prizes" QR code sent in the chat.
  • I saw the QR code on an unofficial website and followed the instructions to scan it using WhatsApp.
  • Give your unlocked phone to someone else to "help me look at something" or "help me connect to the web version".
  • I checked "Stay logged in" on the public computer at the Internet cafe/exhibition, but forgot to log out afterwards.
  • WhatsApp Web sessions in the browser were shared after the computer was infected.

Processing sequence after discovering a strange device

  1. Log out of this device (and all in doubt) immediately.
  2. Check whether you can still control the main mobile phone session; if you have been pushed offline, follow the retrieval process to re-verify your number.
  3. Reset two-step verification.
  4. Review recently clicked links and scanned codes to avoid repeated scams.
  5. Notify contacts who have recently discussed sensitive topics to be alert.

Principles for safe use of PC version

  • Only obtain desktop applications from official channels, or enter the official web address into your browser yourself.
  • The associated actions are only initiated from within the mobile app and will not "force" you to scan from unfamiliar pages.
  • Don’t stay logged in on public devices; when you’re done, go back to the mobile phone and kick it out.
  • It is better to log out of computer sessions that have not been used for a long time.

summary

"Linked Devices" is a list of backdoors to your account. It is not an advanced function page, but a security inspection page. By making checking into a habit, many "I don't know how to get caught" cases can actually be intercepted in the first week.

04-fake-vote-lottery.title: Fake voting, fake lottery, fake support: Don’t trust it even if it is forwarded by acquaintances
04-fake-vote-lottery.excerpt: "Vote for my daughter" messages often come from compromised accounts. Fake websites asking for SMS codes or inducing scans of related codes are a rapidly growing acceptance method in recent years.
04-fake-vote-lottery.body:
Kindness is the most easily weaponized quality in social media. Scammers are very clear: telling you directly "Give me the verification code" will trigger an alarm; but if you change it to "Vote for the children, it only takes ten seconds", many people will click in. Cyber ​​security agencies in Europe and other places have publicly warned: After hackers control the accounts of acquaintances, they send mass voting/competition support requests, and then direct the traffic to counterfeit websites.

How a typical attack unfolds

  1. A scammer has taken control of your friend’s WhatsApp.
  2. You receive a private message or group message from a friend: "Please vote, the deadline is today!" with a link.
  3. The webpage is designed to look like a school, dance competition, or charity voting, requiring you to enter your mobile phone number.
  4. You receive a WhatsApp/SMS verification code on your phone - actually a registration code.
  5. You fill in the code into the web page, and the other party immediately completes the takeover on another device; or
  6. The web page displays a QR code and tells you to "scan the code with WhatsApp to complete your vote", which actually completes the device association.

The first one will make you lose your main account; the second one may allow you to be peeped simultaneously while "your phone is still available". Both are dangerous.

Why previews and pages look so real

Modern fishing will prepare a decent logo, countdown timer, candidate photos, and even do multiple languages. Link preview cards can also be made to look like regular sites. You can’t judge authenticity by “good-looking or not”;what does it ask you to do:

  • Want WhatsApp/SMS verification code? High risk.
  • Do you want you to scan the QR code with a "linked device"? High risk.
  • Requiring you to download an unknown APK to vote? High risk.
  • Want bank card photos and OTP? It has been upgraded from account theft to fraud.

Standard actions when receiving a vote request

  1. Let’s first assume that the other party’s account may have been stolen.
  2. Ask on the phone or in person: "Are you canvassing for votes? Have you sent a link?"
  3. Before confirming, do not click on the link, do not fill in the code, and do not scan the code.
  4. If the other party denies it, remind them to check the associated device and reset the two-step verification.
  5. Report the original message to avoid spreading it in the group.

Real public voting rarely requires you to provide your WhatsApp registration code. Platforms that require login should also use the platform's own account system instead of the "universal mobile phone verification code universal box".

If you have already clicked or filled in

  • After filling in the SMS code: Immediately re-verify your WhatsApp number and regain it, then clear the device and enable two-step verification.
  • Scan the QR code: Immediately go to "Associated Devices" to kick someone.
  • Installation packages have been downloaded: Disable unknown apps, consider anti-virus/reinstall evaluation, and check SMS and accessibility permissions.

How to have a unified voice at home and in the company

It is not enough for one person to be vigilant. Fake voting links are most likely to be forwarded twice in family groups, classmate groups, and company groups. Each forwarding is "whitewashing" the source of the scammers. It is recommended to stick a short rule at the top of the fixed group: "Any link that requires a WhatsApp verification code or scan the code to vote, call first to verify; do not click before verification." The shorter the rule, the easier it is to be followed.

If you are a group administrator, you should delete such messages immediately and remind members to check the associated devices. If the sender is an acquaintance, give priority to using other channels to remind the other party that "your number may have been stolen" instead of just replying "this is a scam" in the original chat - because the person on the other end may not be watching at all.

How to distinguish it from "real voting"

  • Legitimate events will almost never ask you for your WhatsApp registration code.
  • If you need to log in for formal activities, you usually use your own account system instead of the universal "SMS code universal verification".
  • Formal activities will not induce you to use "associated devices" to scan unknown QR codes.
  • Really urgent public welfare/campus voting can also withstand you taking a minute to call and ask yourself.

Shift the burden of "distinguishing authenticity from fake" from "seeing whether the page is beautiful" to "whether it has exceeded its authority to ask for WhatsApp keys." If you think clearly about this step, the vast majority of fake polling stations will reveal their true colors.

summary

The fake voting scam is a combination of "acquaintance + goodwill + short-term operation". Change the rule to:All votes that require QR codes or scan codes must be verified first and disbelieved by default., you can avoid a large class of account hacking paths that are currently very active. Good intentions are worth keeping, but the keys should not be handed over.

05-chain-takeover.title: Serial deception codes of acquaintances: how the address book turns into a chain of transmission
05-chain-takeover.excerpt: If one account is lost, the entire address book is often destroyed along with it. Dismantle the transmission mechanism of serial takeovers and how to cut off the second link.
05-chain-takeover.body:
Viewed in isolation, "sending the verification code to a friend" looks like an oversight; from an attacker's perspective, it is a replicable growth strategy. The patterns reported by the police in Singapore, Malaysia and other places are very similar: the scammer first uses phishing or deceptive codes to get the first number → the victim is squeezed offline → the scammer uses this identity to ask for the "incorrect verification code" from the entire address book → the next victim is tricked → the chain continues. The entire process often completes more than a dozen layers of diffusion within two hours, because the sender at each layer is someone you "know and trust."

Serial deceptive codes are also called "takeover chains" or "address book epidemics." It does not rely on one-time mass advertising, but uses the trust edge of the human network to continuously jump. For the defender, this means:Your safety depends not only on your own discipline, but also on whether there are weak links in your address book——But more importantly, when you are in the "being coded" link, you have the opportunity to become the end of the entire chain.

every role in the chain

  • Entrance 0:The first people to be scammed, phished, or scanned fake voting codes, or whose associated devices were silently hung up. They may not immediately notice that it has been stolen.
  • Propagation node:Each newly taken over account automatically becomes the next wave of "trusted senders". The avatar, nickname, and recent chat context are all real—it’s just that the operator has changed.
  • Filter nodes:Scammers will give priority to privately chatting with contacts, family members, and colleagues they have chatted with recently, and the success rate is much higher than that of cold sales.
  • Monetization node:After accumulating enough accounts, you start to borrow money, ask for bank card screenshots, pay OTP, attract fake investment groups, and convert "trust assets" into cash.

The most critical realization for you is that when you become "the one being coded," you are in the best position to cut the chain. As soon as you refuse, this branch will be broken; as soon as you compromise, your address book will become someone else's ammunition depot.

Why do typical words always deceive people?

The sentence "The verification code was sent in error, read it for me" is effective because it satisfies three psychological buttons at the same time:Acquaintances are trustworthy(The avatar has not changed),mutual aid obligations(Do me a small favor),Extremely simple operation(Copy six numbers). Scammers will also add "Don't tell others" and "I'm in a meeting so it's not convenient for me to make a phone call" to prevent you from using the most effective verification method - voice calls.

In a workplace environment, variations include "Personnel system requires verification code" and "Company VPN registration"; in a home environment, variations include "Hospital registration" and "School registration". The story has changed skin, but the core remains the same: you are asked to hand over the WhatsApp registration code you just received on your phone.

Abnormal signal (even if the avatar is familiar)

  • Suddenly discussing verification codes, OTP, bank card photos, and the front and back of ID cards.
  • The tone is overly eager and prevents you from making phone calls or video calls.
  • Use very uncharacteristic phrasing late at night/at work (too formal or too rushed).
  • Just when I was about to finish coding, I started borrowing money, recruiting groups, and sending investment links.
  • At the same time, multiple friends will tell you "so-and-so is asking for my code" at the same time.
  • The other party says "the number has been changed" but is unwilling to answer your call back using the old number.

House level rules:Anyone who asks for a verification code in WhatsApp will by default assume that "the other party's number may have been stolen." They must call to verify first and never give the code first. This rule applies equally to children, parents, and bosses.

Household and company practices that cut the chain

  1. Build consensus: CAPTCHA request = default scam alert, not an “embarrassed to say no” social occasion.
  2. Use SMS, email or family group (not WhatsApp) to send a group reminder: "Anyone who uses WhatsApp to ask for a password will be treated as if their account has been stolen."
  3. The company's IT or administration prepares a fixed announcement template, pins the abnormal contact person to the top immediately, and designates a person on duty to answer the verification call.
  4. After the victim is recaptured, he must use it in the relevant groupOther verified channelsThe second statement "has been recaptured, and the previous news is invalid."
  5. Regular family/team drills: pretend to be cheaters on each other and practice three rejection lines.

If You Were Stolen: Stop Loss Timeline

In addition to re-verifying the number according to the "Reclaim Process" on this site, please put "Notify Contacts" at the same priority as "Clear Associated Devices". Suggested order:

  1. Reclaim your main session and turn on or reset two-step verification.
  2. Immediately send a group text message to core contacts: "My WhatsApp has just been stolen. Anyone who asks for codes, borrows money, or voting links does not belong to me."
  3. Ask a trusted relative or friend to use other channels to make the announcement on your behalf within your family/colleague group.
  4. Look back at what you posted in the 48 hours before the theft and determine where the chain might extend.
  5. If a relative or friend has transferred money, help them contact the bank and keep the evidence. If necessary, report the case through local police channels.

A common mistake is: thinking "it's over" after taking it back, but not warning the outside world, causing the scammer to continue to borrow money with residual trust before you go online again.

Common misunderstandings

  • Misunderstanding: "The other party is a relative, so it doesn't matter if you give it to me." - Relatives' numbers can also be stolen, and scammers specialize in family links.
  • Misunderstanding: "It's safe if I only give you the code but not the PIN." - The registration code is enough to complete the takeover; the PIN is the second door, and the key cannot be given first.
  • Misunderstanding: "I can just withdraw the message quickly." - The other party's automated script can complete the registration before you react.

summary

Serial deception is not an "accidental interpersonal error", but a structured and scalable communication attack. Training everyone in your address book to be a "denial point" is more important than just strengthening your own phone - because attacks will always come in through the loosest link. Remember: if you refuse to ask for a code once, you may have protected the numbers and money of more than a dozen contacts behind you at the same time.

06-screen-share-scam.title: Screen sharing account theft: Air code capture during video calls
06-screen-share-scam.excerpt: The fake official or banker asks to share your screen and then has a verification code appear on your screen. You didn't "send" the number, but the code has already been read.
06-screen-share-scam.body:
Traditional scam codes require you to type out the numbers and send them to the other party; screen sharing scams omit this step. Scammers use WhatsApp videos, Zoom, Teams and even the system's own "screen sharing" function to establish a "sense of officialdom", and then ask you to share your entire phone screen immediately on the grounds of account unfreezing, tax verification, anti-money laundering inspections, and express delivery claims. Then they instruct you to open a text message, open WhatsApp and log in again, or click on the bank app - the six-digit registration code, payment dynamic password, and even the two-step verification interface will all appear on the other party's screen.

Versions disguised as law enforcement agencies, tax bureaus, central bank customer service, and bank risk control have appeared in police reports from many countries. For users who are not familiar with digital business, this process looks "very professional": there are videos, screenshots of work badges, terminology, and countdown pressure. You may feel that you "didn't send any verification code" throughout the whole process, but the other party has already copied the numbers with their eyes.

Why screen sharing is extra dangerous

  • The lock screen notification banner may display the verification code directly in the share without you having to click on the text message.
  • The other party can guide you to enter "Associated Devices" to scan the QR code, turn off two-step verification, and modify your email address.
  • If you share your computer desktop at the same time, passwords and session cookies saved in the browser may also be exposed.
  • At the end of the scam, the scam often requires the installation of a "remote assistance" app, which is actually a long-term control channel.

Common oppression rhetoric in videos

"If you don't share, your account will be frozen." "If you don't cooperate, you'll be suspected of breaking the law." "IT is remotely rescuing your account." These are all designed to allow you to make a decision within 30 seconds. Formal financial institutions and government departments usually do not complete verification in private WhatsApp videos; when they need to verify identity, they should go through youFind it yourselfThe official App, official website or outlet channels, please refer to the official help center instructions and local formal channels for details.

Defense List (by priority)

  1. Any video call claiming to be official, bank, or platform customer service requires screen sharing: hang up by default.
  2. After hanging up, use the official phone number you saved or the customer service portal in the app to call back instead of the number given in the chat.
  3. If screen sharing is necessary due to work arrangements (such as remote IT troubleshooting), exit banking and instant messaging apps first, turn off lock screen notification previews, and do not click on any verification code-related interfaces during screen sharing.
  4. Teach the elders: "Share screen" and computer screencasting in WeChat/FaceTime are as dangerous to verification codes as "sending codes".

House rules suggestions:Write "video call + screen sharing + mobile phone operation" in red. Elders only need to remember: hang up when they see this group, and let their children take care of the affairs.

If it has been shared and may be leaked

  1. Immediately stop using the share and hang up all remote sessions.
  2. Re-verify the WhatsApp number locally and check the "associated devices".
  3. Reset two-step verification PIN and recovery email; change bank and payment account passwords.
  4. Uninstall suspicious remote control applications and ask professionals to do a physical examination of the device if necessary.
  5. Notify relatives and friends to be alert to unusual messages sent by "you" recently.

Common misunderstandings

  • "I only shared half of the screen and it was fine" - the notification bar verification code is still visible.
  • "The other party is credible if he is wearing a uniform" - the image in the video can be faked.
  • "It's safe if I hang up" - If the code has been taken away, you must take it back immediately and reset the access control.

summary

Air-to-air code retrieval proves: Security not only depends on "whether you are willing to type out the code", but also depends on "who is looking at your screen." Think of screen sharing as a high-privilege operation rather than an ancillary function of video chat; for verification codes, eyes are as much a leakage channel as fingers.

07-call-merge-otp.title: Merge calls and listen to verification codes: Don’t merge strangers into your calls
07-call-merge-otp.excerpt: Scammers trick you into merging three-way calls and letting the line receive a WhatsApp voice verification code - you don't forward the digits, but the code is listened to.
07-call-merge-otp.body:
Phone merging (three-way calls, conference calls) is a daily function, but it has been transformed into a tool for stealing numbers. The techniques used in public reports are generally: Calls from strangers or semi-strangers claiming to be couriers, medical insurance, or school academic affairs offices, saying that they need confirmation from you and the "person in charge"; or pretending that your relatives or friends are in an emergency, asking you to transfer the call to a "lawyer" or "police officer." When you follow the instructions to dial a number and click "Merge Calls", the other end of the line is often a WhatsApp call that has just been initiated.Voice verification call, automatically broadcast the six-digit registration code, and the scammer listens online throughout the process.

This type of scam is especially common among elderly users, because "put him through" sounds like ordinary phone etiquette, and does not involve typing and sending codes in the chat, so the psychological defense line is lower.

How is it different from a scam SMS code?

The SMS code scam relies on you "seeing and forwarding"; the merged call scam relies on you "hearing but not knowing". Sometimes scammers will also ask you to receive a text message code at the same time, and then ask you to "read it to customer service" on the combined line. In essence, you still hand over the registration code to a third party. You may not have entered anything into WhatsApp during the whole process, and you may even think that you are just making a friendly transfer.

The two-part structure of a scam script

  1. bedding:Create an emergency situation (involvement in a case, refund, package being detained) so that you are willing to cooperate with the phone.
  2. fuse:Give you an "official hotline" number to call first and then merge it; this number triggers WhatsApp voice verification or bank OTP voice broadcast.

Be wary of any call asking you to "dial a fixed number first and then merge it together," no matter who the caller claims to be.

Protection rules

  • Do not merge calls with unknown calls; do not help strangers "redirect to the authorities."
  • Urgent matters for relatives and friends: hang up the suspicious line and call the old number in your address book to verify.
  • The WhatsApp voice verification code is as confidential as the SMS code and cannot be spoken to others during any call.
  • If the other party says "Don't hang up, just merge," it's almost always a high-risk sign.

Operator customer service, banks, and WhatsApp officials will not let you "listen to the verification code to complete the verification" through phone merging. If you encounter such statements, please refer to the official help center instructions and do not continue the call.

If you have merged suspicious calls

  1. Immediately check whether WhatsApp is still online and whether you have received the "Already registered on another device" prompt.
  2. If you can still log in: clear the associated device and reset the two-step verification; if you are kicked offline: follow the recapture process to re-verify.
  3. Check with the operator whether call forwarding and unconditional forwarding have been enabled maliciously.
  4. Notify recent contacts: Please be alert if you receive unusual messages from "you".

summary

Do not treat call merging as an operation without security implications. For CAPTCHA scenarios, ears can be just as leaky as eyes. Rejecting unfamiliar mergers and refusing to read codes on the phone are lines of defense that cost almost zero but are often ignored.

Relationship with carrier call forwarding

In addition to merging calls, some scams will also induce you to activate "call forwarding" or "no-answer forwarding" on your mobile phone to forward all future calls to the scammer. The merged call eavesdropping affects the current call; the call transfer affects every future call. If you have ever dialed a special code (such as a function code starting with ** or ##) according to unfamiliar instructions, please call the operator's official customer service immediately to inquire and close all transfers. For details, please refer to the operator's official instructions.

Daily habits can be developed: confirm the service activation status with the operator every few months; when you find that you cannot receive calls from others, put "whether to be transferred" and "whether to change the card" in the same priority list.

08-sim-swap.title: SIM card hijacking and card swapping attacks: When your SMS inbox no longer belongs to you
08-sim-swap.excerpt: After the number is transferred to the new card, the verification code will be entered into the attacker's phone. Understand carrier-side risks and learn to use two-step verification and SIM PIN to reduce harm.
08-sim-swap.body:
SIM swapping (card replacement/number card hijacking) is a more serious attack: the other party uses fake identities, social engineering skills, or exploits loopholes in the operator's process to let the telecommunications company activate your number to a SIM they control. After completion, your phone may suddenly display "No Service", and the SMS OTP that should have been sent to you instead rings on the scammer's phone. WhatsApp uses mobile phone numbers as the primary key, so this is a direct blow to account sovereignty.

If two-step verification is not turned on, the other party can re-register after receiving the SMS code; even if you turn on two-step verification, you will immediately fall into a two-line race between "the operator takes back the number" and "WhatsApp takes back the session." High-profile public figures are long-term targets, but ordinary users may also be selected based on their business accounts, investment groups, or simply the quality of their address books.

Possible signs

  • The phone is out of service for a long time for no reason, the airplane mode switch is invalid, or it prompts "SIM not inserted".
  • Suddenly I can't receive any text messages, but the bank prompts me to log in abnormally.
  • WhatsApp prompts that the number has been registered on other devices.
  • Relatives and friends receive money loan messages from "you", but your phone cannot open WhatsApp at all.
  • The operator sent you a notification that the card replacement was successful, but you did not handle it.

First time emergency (in order)

  1. Use another mobile phone or landline to call the operator's official customer service (according to the channel on the official app, official website or bill) to report an abnormal card change and request a freeze on the transfer and a replacement SIM.
  2. After the number is restored, immediately re-verify WhatsApp on this machine and clear the associated devices.
  3. Notify banks and payment platforms to pay attention to abnormal OTPs and transfers; reset key account passwords.
  4. Text your friends and family not to trust any recent WhatsApp loan requests.
  5. Keep operator work orders and text message records, and report the case to local police channels when necessary.

Daily risk reduction measures

  • Ask your operator whether you can set additional passwords for card replacement/transfer or restrictions on going to the office.
  • Enable a PIN for the SIM to prevent the physical card from being directly inserted and used by others.
  • WhatsApp must enable two-step verification and bind your email address.
  • For important financial accounts, App tokens and hardware keys are preferred instead of text messages alone.
  • Avoid disclosing complete mobile phone number, ID card information and address combination on social platforms.

The card swap attack targets "who controls the SMS inbox". Carrier side lock + WhatsApp two-step verification + loss of contact plan, a three-piece set is indispensable.

Review after recapture

Check whether the scammer has completed WhatsApp registration on your number or sent a group of fraudulent messages. If so, you need to use other channels to clarify and help relatives and friends who have been defrauded to stop the payment. Consider whether to temporarily increase monitoring of high-value accounts associated with numbers.

summary

SIM hijacking upgrades the mobile phone number from "contact information" to "security root". Establishing the conditioned reflex of "sudden no service = highest alarm" saves time than fighting for the number afterwards.

Linkage risks with banks and email addresses

After successfully changing the card, the attacker will not only target WhatsApp, but may also reset bank SMS verification and email password retrieval in the same window. Therefore, while declaring the operator, take the initiative to call the bank customer service to explain the situation, freeze abnormal channels, and check the mailbox remote login record. Treat "mobile phone number loss" as an account matrix-level event rather than a single App failure.

09-phishing-sites.title: Fake official websites and phishing links: don’t click if they look like it
09-phishing-sites.excerpt: From the pressure of domain names and words to "what do you want to do", the system teaches you how to expose fake login pages. When you need the web version, just use the official address you entered yourself.
09-phishing-sites.body:
The essence of phishing attacks is to forge trust symbols that you are familiar with: Meta green, lock icon, customer service language, countdown, and even domain name spelling that is almost the same as the real website. The attacker does not need to break WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption. He only needs to trick you into entering your mobile phone number and six-digit registration code at a fake "login counter" or downloading a shell app, and then hand over your account keys.

In recent years, phishing pages have also evolved a "progressive" process: they first ask you to fill in your mobile phone number to "make an appointment to unblock", and then you actually receive the official SMS code a few seconds later - you mistakenly think that the process is formal, so you fill in the code you just received on the fake site. The success of the attack lies in the fact that users mistook “receiving real text messages” for “the website is real.”

Common delivery channels

  • Short links and "Account will be permanently banned" banners in WhatsApp private chats and group messages.
  • SMS/email pretending to be WhatsApp Business review, refund, HD call activation.
  • Fake "WhatsApp Web Login" site on search engine advertising space.
  • The "official announcement" and fake update package forwarded by the stolen account.

Four self-checks before clicking on the button

  1. Am I doing this in the first place? The unexpected "Account will be blocked if not verified within 24 hours" is highly suspicious.
  2. Is the domain name in the browser address bar the domain name I typed in myself? Be wary of whatsapp-verify, wa-login, multiple hyphens, and strange suffixes.
  3. Does the page ask for registration code, bank OTP, mnemonic phrase, and remote desktop? Either one should exit.
  4. Do you want to induce APK downloads, description files, or enable accessibility/screen recording? Commonly found in Android side Trojan chains.

The only way to safely open the web version/PC version

Open the browser yourself, enter the official domain name manually or use the official desktop client; initiate "Associate Device" in WhatsApp on your mobile phone and scan the QR code. Never log in from the blue link in the chat. The QR code on the scan page can only come fromThe official page you just opened, you cannot scan pictures sent by others in the chat.

Write "the official entrance must be built by yourself" as muscle memory: the link handed over by others can only be used as a reference, not as an entrance.

Grading after wrong clicks

  • Browse only:Close the page, do not click twice; be wary of follow-up calls.
  • Registration code filled in:Immediately re-verify the number locally, clear the device, and reset the two-step verification.
  • Bank card/email password handed in:If you need to change the password of the corresponding account urgently, contact the bank; check the remote login rules by email.
  • Unknown APK installed:Disconnect the network and uninstall, restore to factory settings if necessary, and re-login and reinforce each platform.

Report the screenshot of the phishing link to WhatsApp and give a brief warning in the group to reduce chain casualties.

summary

Encryption protects the transmission, not your hand walking into the fake counter. Self-made domain name, self-checking of behavior, and withdrawal upon requesting the code - these three tricks can stop most phishing at the door.

Identify the combination of "real preview and fake web page"

The link preview in the chat can show the thumbnail of the regular domain name, but the actual jump is to another address. Long press the link to view the full URL, or copy it to Notes to check before deciding whether to open it. On iOS/Android, beware of the redirection chain of "click domain name A for the first time, and then follow domain name B for the second time."

10-recover-account.title: The whole process of recovering an account after being stolen: follow the official logic step by step
10-recover-account.excerpt: Re-using your own number to complete the registration verification is the key to kicking others away. This article is written in order to recapture, clear equipment, notify relatives and friends, and avoid a second loss.
10-recover-account.body:
When people find out that WhatsApp has been stolen, their first reaction is often confusion: they want to report it, they want to find someone to do it for them, and they are asked by their relatives and friends, "Is it you who borrowed money just now?" Please slow down first - according to the public instructions in the WhatsApp Help Center, when the problem is "Someone is using your number",On your own secure primary phone, use this number to complete the registration verification again, is the core step to remove illegal sessions. After correctly entering the SMS or voice registration code you received, the other party's use on the main device will usually be pushed offline.

This process is not guaranteed to be completed in one minute: you may also have to deal with unfamiliar two-step verification PINs, clean up associated devices, and announce stop losses to the outside world. Doing them in sequence saves more time than trying them in parallel.

Recapture the First 60 Seconds: Four Questions

  • Can I still open WhatsApp? If you can open it, clear the "associated devices" first, and don't rush to chat with scammers.
  • Have I been kicked back to the registration page? If so, you will directly enter the re-inspection process.
  • Is it possible that the phone is poisoned or remotely controlled? If so, disconnect the internet and kill the virus first, otherwise you will lose it again if you take it back.
  • Are you experiencing no signal when changing cards at the same time? Contact the operator first and then talk about app recapture.

Standard recapture steps

  1. existTrusted nativeReinstall or open official WhatsApp (only official store sources).
  2. Enter your complete mobile phone number in international format to request a registration code.
  3. Cover the screen when receiving codes.no waySend to anyone; enter this.
  4. If a two-step verification PIN is required: enter the one you remember; if it is an unfamiliar PIN, see the topic on this site, but you should still complete the SMS verification to kick the person first.
  5. After logging in → Settings → Connected devices → Exit all unknown items.
  6. Turn off and on two-step verification, change your PIN, and confirm that the recovery email is still yours.
  7. Check whether privacy and security related settings have been tampered with; exclude unofficial clients.

Counter-intuitive but important: Just changing the 2-step verification PIN won’t single out the logged-in scammer; re-verifying the number is key. Also do not blindly perform operations such as "report your account" before recapturing it to avoid interfering with the recovery. Please refer to the official help center guidelines for details.

External communication during the recapture

Do two things in parallel: kick people technically and stop the bleeding interpersonally.

  • Notify family members via SMS/call: “I” asked for money and passwords on WhatsApp in the past 24 hours.
  • Ask trusted colleagues to send the company group statement on their behalf through non-WhatsApp channels.
  • If a transfer has already occurred, instruct the injured party to immediately contact the bank to stop the payment, retain evidence of the chat, and report the case through local police channels as appropriate.

Reinforcement 24–72 hours after recapture

  1. Check the associated devices again and enable App Lock.
  2. Review of lost points: Fishing? An acquaintance wants to code? Fake vote? Share screen?
  3. Synchronize your "core rules" with core contacts (for example, you must call when borrowing money).
  4. If the business account is stolen, customer notifications will be issued according to business topics.

Common mistakes

  • Send the registration code to a "retrieval agent" stranger - stolen twice.
  • The recapture was successful but no announcement was made, and relatives and friends continued to be fooled.
  • Only changing the password does not clear the associated device, but the web page is still synchronized.

summary

Regain the order of fighting: first number sovereignty, then clear the back door, then stop losses in interpersonal relationships, and finally review and strengthen. Collecting this article as an emergency card is more reliable than searching hastily.

11-unknown-pin-7days.title: Encountering an unfamiliar 2-step verification PIN: Wait, kick, and reset your strategy
11-unknown-pin-7days.excerpt: A thief may be able to set a PIN first. Explain why SMS code verification is still critical, how to follow the official process when you don’t know your PIN, and what to do during the waiting period.
11-unknown-pin-7days.body:
Two-step verification is supposed to be a shield, but it may be installed on your account by attackers and become a wall blocking you. When re-registering, many victims find that the system requires them to enter a two-step verification PIN, but they have never set it up - this means that someone has controlled the number and enabled two-step verification, or it may even have been bound to the attacker's recovery email.

At this time, be sure not to panic and look for a "PIN brushing" service; that is a secondary fraud. The official logic in public information is:SMS/phone registration codeProve you have a mobile phone number;PINis an additional password. The two systems have to solve different problems.

Let’s first distinguish between the two types of “codes”

  • Registration code:A six-digit text message or voice code sent to a mobile phone. Once entered, illegal sessions on other devices are often pushed offline.
  • 2-Step Verification PIN:A 6-digit password set earlier by you or the attacker. If you do not know and cannot restore via email, the system may require you to wait for a period of time (a common public description is about 7 days at most) before continuing, subject to specific App prompts.

Key takeaways:Don’t give up on entering your registration code just because you’re stuck on your PIN. By completing the number verification first, you can often remove the other party's immediate operation rights.

If you remember your PIN and email

  1. Enter the PIN normally; or follow the official retrieval process via email.
  2. Immediately change your PIN and recovery email after logging in.
  3. Clear associated devices and check whether any abnormal group messages remain.

If the PIN is completely unknown

  1. You still need to complete the registration code verification to regain control of your phone.
  2. Follow the interface prompts to handle PIN waiting or email appeal; do not disclose the registration code to strangers.
  3. While waiting, continue to send text messages/phone calls to warn family and friends: any WhatsApp messages cannot be trusted.
  4. Confirm that the SIM card has not been changed again; strengthen the main email account.
  5. Log in as soon as possible after waiting and set upOnly you knownew PIN and email address.

It’s hard to wait seven days, but it’s part of official risk control. It is more reliable to use this time to stop loss notifications and collect evidence than to find a "second-breaking PIN".

Forced actions after regaining control

  • New PIN + loginable recovery email; old PIN is invalid.
  • Clear and review associated devices; application lock is enabled.
  • Review how the account was initially lost to avoid malicious PIN setting on the 8th day.

summary

Unfamiliar PINs are suffocating, but the path is still there: kicking people with registration codes, dealing with PINs according to official rules, stopping the bleeding externally during the waiting period, and rebuilding access control after returning. Patience and sequence are safer than shortcuts.

How to accompany family members during the waiting period

The seven-day wait is especially torturous for the elders. Children should briefly synchronize the progress twice a day and emphasize "don't look for scalpers." At the same time, we help elders temporarily migrate their important contacts to phone messages to prevent scammers from continuing to impersonate them. You can write the prompt copy in the official app on paper to prevent them from mistaking the fake customer service in the chat.

The first thing to complete after waiting is not to send the status, but to change the PIN, change the email, and clean the device - the order cannot be messed up.

Tips for Helping Your Children

If parents are stuck with an unfamiliar PIN, their children should accompany them through the official process remotely instead of trying "third-party convenient unlocking". Help parents contact old colleagues through text messages and explain that WhatsApp is temporarily unavailable to prevent the scam from continuing. Keep the work order number of the operator and mailbox service provider, and reinforce it once after the waiting period is over, which is less likely to be missed than sporadic encryption changes.

12-signs-of-compromise.title: A complete collection of abnormal account signals: How to detect theft or synchronization as early as possible
12-signs-of-compromise.excerpt: From sudden logouts, unfamiliar associated devices, to feedback from friends that you are asking for code - classify early warning signals and provide corresponding actions.
12-signs-of-compromise.body:
Discovering the theft an hour earlier often means one less round of relatives and friends being defrauded and one less transfer. Many cases are not "unpreventable", but are regarded as "little bugs" or "misunderstandings by friends" when the signals appear. Think of the following grading list as an inspection instrument. When the corresponding color appears, perform the corresponding action instead of waiting for "ironclad evidence" before remediating.

Red signal: act now

  • Forced to exit without any operation, or prompted that the number has been registered on another device.
  • You didn't click to log in, but you received multiple registration verification codes in succession.
  • Browsers, cities, and device names that have never been seen before appear in the associated device list.
  • Multiple friends reported at the same time: You are asking for a verification code or urging a transfer.
  • You chat online, but the other party says "you" and replies with different content on the other end.

action:Re-verify your number immediately → Clear all associations → Reset two-step verification → Notify relatives and friends via text message.

Orange signal: must be processed that day

  • A preview of an unknown chat reply flashed in the notification bar, but you didn't send it when you opened the conversation.
  • A group friend sent a private message asking: Is the link just sent yours?
  • It is found that two-step verification has been turned off, or the recovery email address has been changed (if visible).
  • After borrowing/clicking on the phone, the phone experienced abnormal power consumption and unfamiliar auxiliary functions were turned on.

action:Check all associated devices; reset two-step verification; check recent click records and installation sources; inform close contacts to be vigilant.

Yellow signal: Increase the frequency of inspections

  • Frequently receiving "official warnings" from external links is not done by you actively.
  • Semi-acquaintances repeatedly tried to see if they could borrow money or help scan QR codes.
  • I used the web version in a hotel/internet cafe and am not sure if I have logged out.
  • After I changed my card abroad, my text messages were delayed, and I was worried that my OTP would be intercepted by others.

action:Check related equipment every day this week; refuse to click on unfamiliar links; review after returning to China in the travel topic.

Treat "friend feedback" as the highest priority

When a friend says, "You are asking for my code," don't argue that it's "impossible," but check your device and session first. The cost of misjudgment is low, but the cost of missed judgment is high. If the self-examination fails, ask your friends to give a brief warning in the group to prevent a chain reaction.

Set up a "red phone": Make an agreement with two relatives and friends to call each other to confirm if there is any abnormality in the account, without replying via WhatsApp.

Recording and Evidence Collection

If an orange or above signal appears, screenshots can be associated with the device page, verification code text message time, and suspicious chats to facilitate future evidence through bank or police channels. Do not frequently click on phishing links to "confirm whether they are fake".

summary

Signal classification is to avoid the two extremes of numbness and panic. Treating a question from a friend as a fire alarm can often stop the attack before the realization stage.

Create a personal "exception log"

Use a mobile phone memo or a paper notebook to record the date and screenshot number of every abnormal verification code, unfamiliar device, and friend’s question. If you need to explain the timeline to a bank or law enforcement agency in the future, organized evidence is more powerful than fragmented memories. The log itself does not contain sensitive codes, only event types are recorded.

The balance between false positives and false negatives

Sometimes friends forget that they have just sent a strange link and will falsely report that you have been hacked. Even so, lightweight self-checking (associated devices, recent login prompts) is still a low-cost action. The loss of one missed report is far greater than the 30 seconds spent checking several times. It is recommended to "spot check" each other with your friends every quarter: ask "Have you received any suspicious messages impersonating me recently?"

13-friend-asks-money.title: Borrow money from friends, change numbers, keep it confidential: complete verification manual
13-friend-asks-money.excerpt: The first step to monetize a stolen account is often to borrow money from the address book. Teach you a verification process that does not hurt feelings and can prevent transfer fraud.
13-friend-asks-money.body:
The most common "cold start monetization" after account hacking is to borrow money from the address book. Scammers don't send messages in general. Instead, they read historical chats, imitate your name, mannerisms, and recent topics, and write a private message saying "an old classmate is asking for help" and "the project is short of payment." What you have to guard against is not whether your friends will lend you money, but whetherWhether this request passed the unforgeable core.

High-risk speech characteristics

  • Emphasize immediately, keep it confidential, don’t let family members know, and prevent third parties from getting involved.
  • He claimed that his phone was broken and his number had been changed, and he asked to add a new number and transfer money immediately.
  • Reject or delay video exposure; voice may also be imitated by AI (see the AI ​​topic on this site).
  • The payment methods suddenly changed to gift cards, USDT, unfamiliar QR codes, and multiple small payments.
  • First, a small amount is "tested" and then a large amount is added.

Recommended verification process (it’s okay to be stubborn)

  1. Stop talking about money in the original chat and say "I'll call to confirm" - a true friend will understand.
  2. Call the address bookOld number that has been stored for a long time, without the new number just issued by the other party.
  3. Ask for two non-public details that only you know (where you met last week, family code).
  4. If still unsure, contact your spouse/colleague to cross-check.
  5. Any reminder "too late to place orders/surgery fees" cannot replace the verification; for large amounts, delay in arrival can be agreed upon.

A true friend rarely shames your discretion when questioned. Forcing you to "stop asking so many questions and transfer first" is more like a scam script trying to grab the window.

What should I do if it has been transferred out?

  1. Contact the bank/payer immediately to attempt to block or dispute.
  2. Save chats, transfer vouchers, counterparty numbers and timelines.
  3. Inform the friend who was defrauded that his account may have been stolen, and report the case through local police channels. Whether it needs to be determined by the case handling agency.
  4. Give a brief warning in the mutual friend group to avoid secondary harm.

Family and Company Covenant Template

"Any emergency loan requested through the chat app must be confirmed by voice or in person; no transfer will be made without confirmation." Write this sentence into the employee handbook and pin it to the top of the family WeChat group.

summary

The verification process is the insurance of friendship, not distrust. The friend who was stolen also needs you to help him prevent more victims.

"Batch borrowing" in group chat

Hackers sometimes post loan templates to multiple groups at the same time, using someone to transfer money first to create a herd mentality. Seeing that many people in the group have transferred does not mean that I have confirmed that I need to be independent. If the administrator discovers an abnormality, he or she should temporarily ban all members and verify via telephone channels.

Company financial regulations: Any change to the collection account must be accompanied by a stamped PDF and a phone call. Screenshots of the chat cannot be used as a basis alone.

Pitfalls of small-amount test transfers

The scammer first asks the victim to transfer tens of dollars to "confirm friendship", and then adds a larger amount. The rule should be: regardless of the amount, the verification standards should be the same. Don’t skip phone confirmation just because “the amount is small”. Some scripts are designed to accumulate small amounts and avoid bank risk control thresholds.

Couple and partnership business

Romantic relationships and partners are more likely to transfer money due to "embarrassment to verify". Agreement: All partnership funds will be made through company accounts and written emails, and decisions will not be made through personal WhatsApp. During a breakup or dispute, you should be especially wary of pretending to be the other person to borrow money. The stronger the relationship, the harder the process must be. This is a protective relationship.

14-privacy-settings.title: Complete reinforcement of privacy settings: Reduce personal information used by social workers
14-privacy-settings.excerpt: Avatar, last seen online, group invitation, status visible range... the recommended values ​​are explained one by one. Privacy settings don’t replace two-step verification, but they can reduce scammers’ fodder.
14-privacy-settings.body:
End-to-end encryption protects the confidentiality of messages during transmission and does not automatically hide your avatar, signature, online time, or group exposure. Scammers will collect these fragments and put together a more believable script: they know that you have just left the country, know that your daughter is participating in the competition, and know the names you commonly use. Tightening privacy is a low-cost task to reduce the area of ​​social work materials.

It is recommended to adjust item by item (Settings → Privacy)

  • avatar:Be restrained from non-contacts and reduce the number of strangers cloning your image.
  • Last online and online:Restrict on demand to reduce being tracked.
  • about:Do not write down your mobile phone number, address, class schedule, or the full name of your child’s school.
  • state:Control the audience; status will still spread if forwarded, evaluate before sending.
  • Group:"Who can add me to the group" is recommended as "My Contacts" to prevent strangers from joining the group.
  • call:Options such as muting unknown calls (depending on version) to reduce harassment.
  • Read receipt:Experience the feature; the security core is still in the verification code and device.

Step by step operating habits

Every time you change an item, use another trumpet or a friend's non-contact account to test what strangers can see. You can scan again every month after changing your phone or after a major event (wedding, travel), as app updates sometimes restore the default, more open options.

The boundary between privacy and theft prevention

Tightening privacy won't save "you take the initiative to send a verification code", but it can save cold start scammers half the script material. It is at a different level from two-step verification and associated device inspection, and needs to be stacked rather than replaced.

When changing the privacy of elders, give priority to the three items of "group invitation restrictions + hiding avatars from non-contacts + removing sensitive information from the about column", which is cost-effective.

Extra points for business number

  • Store avatars can be counterfeited, so public announcements must use consistent brand payment information across multiple channels.
  • After an employee leaves, check who can still send messages on behalf of the brand account.

summary

Spending fifteen minutes to go through the privacy page is a low-cost "version of the story to reduce being deceived." Cooperating with verification code discipline can truly blunt the scammer's words.

Recommended files for different groups of people

Elders: Group invitations are limited to contacts, avatars are limited to contacts, and closed status is displayed to the public. Teenagers: Limit visibility during online time and reduce entry points for strangers to send messages. Business ID: The avatar and "About" are used for business display, but avoid writing personal addresses; payment information uses fixed template messages instead of random verbal changes.

After each major version update of the App, the privacy default value may be changed, and another round of inspection should be carried out after changing devices or updating.

Screenshots and external files

Your avatar and signature may have been screenshotted and spread by others. Regularly check whether your mobile phone number + avatar combination appears in search engines and human flesh sites. If found, you can appeal to the platform for deletion. Privacy settings are to reduce new leaks, not to recover leaked material; but it is still worth doing.

Side effects of syncing contacts

Allowing WhatsApp to read the address book will upload the numbers of relatives and friends for friend discovery. If your device is stolen, this address book also becomes an attack list. You can turn off contact uploading in privacy (subject to version options) and add core contacts manually instead. When the operation path changes, check the official help center for instructions.

Summary retelling

Privacy is a speed bump, not a moat; it, together with verification code discipline and equipment lists, constitutes complete protection. Note the date when you complete the setup and review it six months later.

15-official-app-only.title: Only use official WhatsApp: Risks of modding packages and non-store installation
15-official-app-only.excerpt: The so-called prevention of withdrawal, multiple openings, and membership cracking may be backdoors. Explain why official channel updates are so important and how to self-check the current installation source.
15-official-app-only.body:
WhatsApp’s official security instructions have repeatedly emphasized that unofficial or modified clients may lead to account theft, blocking, or continued leaks. The so-called "anti-withdrawal", "double-open", "theme cracking" and "hidden online" APKs are often hidden under the shell of legitimate functions, with additional permissions - read notifications, barrier-free clicks, automatic forwarding of verification codes - once the endpoint is compromised, end-to-end encryption cannot protect the registration code you actively display on the screen.

High-risk source identification

  • APK distributed through group files, network disks, and forum short links.
  • The names are similar to WhatsApp Plus, GB, Delta and other forks; the icons are slightly different.
  • The installation wizard asks to turn off Play Protect and open unknown sources.
  • Requires login to WhatsApp and full management of text messages.

Correct installation path

  1. iOS App Store only, developer should be WhatsApp LLC.
  2. Android gives priority to Google Play or the official version of the official store of the mobile phone manufacturer.
  3. Download the desktop version from Meta's official guide and do not search for third-party "acceleration packages".
  4. Enable automatic system updates to patch known vulnerabilities.

Self-examination and migration

Check the developer and reviews on the store page to see if there are any unusual fraudulent orders, and whether the permission list is excessive. If you have used the modified version for a long time:

  1. Back up necessary chats; uninstall unofficial clients.
  2. Install the official version and re-verify your number.
  3. Clear associated devices, reset two-step verification, and change PIN.
  4. If a Trojan is suspected: perform an anti-virus or reset assessment on the premise that the device is safe.

"Free premium features" are often exchanged: you save the subscription fee, and the scammer gets your entire account and address book.

Promote words within the organization

In the company training, "Modifying WhatsApp means bringing in a backdoor" is written as an IT red line and is tested together with phishing identification.

summary

The official client is the foundation for all security assumptions. The foundation is wrong, the two-step verification above is just psychological comfort.

Enterprise MDM and dual-opener

Some employees use company MDM or third-party "dual application opening" to log in to two WhatsApps on one work phone. If the source of the dual-open device is unknown, it is also possible to hijack the notification bar verification code. Enterprise IT should whitelist only official package names and prohibit sideloading; employees' personal computers should also avoid installing forks to save trouble.

Correct posture when update fails

If the official store update fails repeatedly, do not download the forum "full package" instead. You should clear the store cache, check the system time, and contact official support channels. Temporarily using the web version to reply is also safer than installing an unfamiliar APK - the web version also abides by the associated device rules.

Second-hand mobile phone pre-installation trap

When buying a second-hand Android phone, check whether it has unofficial WhatsApp pre-installed or comes with resident apps such as "acceleration" and "cleanup". Only install from the official store after factory reset. If the seller claims to have "already logged in for you", resolutely log in again and change your PIN.

Summary retelling

Every modding attempt is a bet that your address book is worth more than a few bells and whistles. The one who wins the bet is always the liar.

Remember: the original version is free, modification is the most expensive.

16-phone-lock-physical.title: Mobile phone lock screen and physical security: preventing people around you from stealing connections
16-phone-lock-physical.excerpt: Many web version failures occur during "just a minute of viewing". Strong screen lock, notification preview policy and post-borrowing inspection form the physical layer defense line.
16-phone-lock-physical.body:
The unlocked phone at the table is often underestimated in discussions of digital theft. Operate on behalf of a repair shop, pick it up jokingly with colleagues, "help me log into the web version" from family members, leave the dinner table to go to the bathroom - attackers do not need remote skills. As long as they complete a code scan within tens of seconds, the associated device session can synchronize your messages for a long time.

Basic configuration list

  • System lock screen: Prioritize long passwords or complex PINs, and use biometrics as a convenient layer to avoid easy-to-guess patterns.
  • Set the automatic screen lock time to the shortest acceptable interval (e.g. 30 seconds – 1 minute).
  • Lock screen notifications hide verification codes and chat content previews.
  • If you enable app lock (fingerprint/face) in WhatsApp, you still need to verify it again after unlocking the phone.
  • Sensitive group chats can be overlaid with chat locks (see related topics).

Borrowing and repair scenarios

  1. Don’t leave your unlocked phone with others alone, even for a minute.
  2. If you are present when others are required to operate, prohibit them from entering the "Associated Devices" or system VPN/Profile page.
  3. The first thing you do when you get your phone back is to open the list of associated devices and remove the unfamiliar entries.
  4. Before sending for repair, exit WhatsApp or make sure to lock the screen + turn off notifications; ask the store in writing not to browse personal privacy.

Shoulder view of public environment

Please block the registration code when entering it in the subway or airport; turn off automatic reading notifications. The attacker can also obtain OTP by using naked eye shoulder peek + video recording.

Before lending your phone, you can manually lock the screen. Politeness and a five-minute explanation are better than taking back your account afterwards.

Stolen cell phone

After the device is physically lost, in addition to reporting the loss to the police and the operator, recheck WhatsApp with a new device as soon as possible (the SIM is still yours), clear the association, and change the PIN. If the SIM is also on board, priority will be given to replacing the card.

summary

Physical security is the floor of digital security. If the floor is gone, no matter how high you stand, you will fall.

Children and nanny at home scene

Children will swipe notifications out of curiosity, and housekeeping staff may answer calls on their behalf. In addition to app lock, family members can be educated not to read out verification codes in front of minors. For reasonable needs such as the nanny borrowing a mobile phone to take pictures, the camera mode can be used instead of unlocking the desktop directly.

If smart watches and tablets log in with the same number and forward text messages, they must also be included in the scope of physical inspection.

Wearable device risks

When a smartwatch synchronizes to display WhatsApp notifications, the verification code may also be exposed on the wrist. In outdoor running and gym scenes, sensitive previews on the watch should be turned off, or OTP text messages should be temporarily muted to the wearable layer. Borrowing someone else's watch to log in to the same account will also leave traces of the session and should be evaluated independently.

Camera physical blocking habits

Video call scams sometimes direct you to switch to a front-facing camera display. Develop the habit of turning off camera permissions or physical sliders when not in use to reduce the chance of being induced to show your bank card or ID card desktop. Parents should be present for spot checks when their children use tablet video classes.

Summary retelling

Think of the lock screen as a belt and the app lock as a pocket buckle; if the belt is not fastened, the pocket buckle is useless. Both are in place at the same time.

When charging before going to bed, do not put your unlocked phone next to guests who are out of reach on the bedside; when dining, place your phone face down to reduce the exposure of verification code pop-ups.

Do not use an image containing a photo of your home address as the lock screen wallpaper to avoid leaking it if you lose your phone.

17-whatsapp-web-safety.title: WhatsApp Web and PC: long rules for safe use
17-whatsapp-web-safety.excerpt: From the official entrance, keep logged in option, public computer process to abnormal session handling, a complete specification is given to people who often reply to messages on the computer.
17-whatsapp-web-safety.body:
The computer allows us to respond to customers and family members faster, but it also exposes conversations to "larger screens, longer login times, and more shared environments."
